# beowulf-fitt-30 — review, Pass 1

Reviewer: adversarial, Pass 1. `units.json` edited in place by script; no `t` changed (checked equal before and after). Sources used: Klaeber's text and apparatus, the packet, the published parts (grep of `beowulf-*.json`). No modern translation opened or recalled.

Checks that passed without change: the first unit's note carries the 2039/2093 boundary sentence; every unit has a note; ‘…’ quoting is used throughout; brackets (`[gūð]sele`), parentheses and the three italics (ondlēan, gomenwudu, grimne) are explained; no dot-under vowel occurs in the part, so no explanation is owed; cross-references checked against the source lines: 124, 443, 750, 1065, 1138, 1323, 1359, 1497, 1513, 1518, 1541, 1567, 2002, 2034, 2138 all true.

## Changes

| line · field | severity | what was wrong | what was done |
|---|---|---|---|

| 2098 · n | medium | Note did not account for `sīo swīðre` standing far from `hand`. | Says it agrees with `hand` across the verb and that `l` keeps that order. |

## Findings considered and refused

- 2093 · n/`l` "the manuscript reads ‘huiedā’": the apparatus line is "MS. A huiedā", which gives the manuscript reading as transcribed; left as written.
- 2093 · i "scourge of the people" for `lēodsceaða`: faithful to "people-scather"; left.
- 2120 · i "That monstrous woman" against `l` "A monstrous woman": the woman was named in the previous sentence, `l` is literal, English idiom needs the definite; no sense lost.
- 2122 · i "was going out of": `ūðgenge` is an adjective ("departing"), `l` has "departing", the progressive agrees; left.
- 2127 · i pluperfect "had carried" for `ætbær`: the carrying precedes the morning in the previous sentence, as `geseten hæfdon` does at 2104; left.
- 2127 · n whose "fiend" `fēondes` is (mother or Grendel): the apparatus gives nothing; I will not add an unsupported claim.
- 2131 · n "past subjunctive" for `efnde`, `genēðde`, `fremede`: the weak preterite is the same in indicative; the label is the syntactic one after `þæt` of request, and true as such; left.
- 2124 · l "Neither they him were allowed": the `ne` is carried by "Neither" (double negation in the OE); a second "not" would be gibberish; left.
- 2115 · `nīode nāman` "eagerly took … took our pleasure": already flagged as a guess in the note; left.
- 2113 · i "heart" for `hreðer`: note says "breast, heart"; left.
- 2099 · `hēan` as "humbled": Klaeber's sense; left.
- 2142 · n closing sentence ("The sentence ends at the full stop of 2143"): factual, not an aphorism; left.
- Dots under vowels: none in this part, so the "first dot" sentence is not owed.

# beowulf-fitt-30 — review, Pass 2

Reviewer: adversarial, Pass 2, independent re-read of every note, `l` and `i` against the Old English, then every `gloss.json` entry against its line(s) and `known-forms.json`. `units.json` and `gloss.json` edited in place by script; `t` unchanged (asserted before write). Cross-references re-checked against the source lines (443, 824, 1065, 1138, 1323, 1324, 1359, 1449, 1497, 1513, 1518, 1541, 1567, 1590, 1724, 2002 all true). Pass-1 edits introduced no errors. All 12 `__broaden__` entries were verified as old entry whole + " · " + new reading; 4 more were added (below). No new entry exceeds 260 characters (longest 195).

## Changes — text

| line · field | severity | what was wrong | what was done |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2129 · l | medium | "of those which the people-chief long had befallen" reads in English as the chief doing the befalling; the note (correctly) takes `lēodfruman` as the object. | "of those which long had befallen the people-chief". |
| 2111 · n | medium | `gioguðe` called "genitive or accusative": the -e is the genitive/dative ending of `geoguð` (accusative would be `geoguð`), and `cwīðan` is usually construed with the genitive. | Note now says genitive-or-dative -e, `cwīðan` usually with the genitive, `hildestrengo` -o the nominative/accusative form (not regular genitive `strenge`), taken as second object, case of the pair not settled. |
| 2138 · n | low | `hine hēafde becearf` (1590) is rendered "cut him off from his head" in beowulf-fitt-23, the same construction as here; the note did not mention it, so the reader could not see the choice. | Note cites 1590, allows that `hēafde` may be a dative of what is cut off, and says "at the head" is kept because the poem has her struck, not beheaded. `l`/`i` left. |
| 2141 · n | low | "the lexica also give ‘timid’ for it in other writers": not supported by anything in the packet, unverifiable here. | Clause removed. |

## Findings considered and refused

- 2113 `worn` as "a multitude" and `i` "so much": matches known entry (worn, multitude) and the sense; left.
- 2124 · l "Neither they him were allowed": kept, as in pass 1 (double negation).
- 2127 · i "had carried": kept, as in pass 1.
- 2131 · `ðīne līfe` crux: the convention says a famous crux goes to `QUESTIONS.md`; this reviewer was told to edit only units.json and gloss.json, so it is reported to the caller instead (no entry exists in QUESTIONS.md yet).
- 2131 · l "noble-deed" for `eorlscipe` (published 1724 has "noble rank"): different sense in context (a deed performed with `efnde`), note explains "a hero’s deeds"; left.
- 2105 · gloss felafricgende: lemma shown as `fricgan` with the compound explained in the remark; acceptable form, left.
- grundhyrde, scilding, scildunga glosses name Grendel's mother / Hrothgar in the remark: identities, not line numbers; left.
- gemǣne, fela, grētte known entries: their stated parses cover the use here (nominative singular feminine; adverbial/noun fela; 3rd singular preterite); no broadening.
- 2093 · "manuscript reads huiedā": apparatus "MS. A", left as in pass 1.
